extracted_definitions.definition: The frequency at which follow-up visits should occur
extracted_definitions.source_excerpt: The follow-up frequency suggested in the first 5 years is every 6 months or earlier if any symptoms. Subsequent visits could be annual up to10 years and then 2 yearly.
extracted_definitions.scope_rationale: This definition is specific to the supportive specialty for breast cancer and outlines the recommended follow-up schedule.

extracted_definitions.definition: Patients with significant family history of cancer or known BRCA mutation
extracted_definitions.source_excerpt: Patients with significant family history of cancer or known BRCA mutation should be kept on lifelong 6 monthly or annual follow up
extracted_definitions.scope_rationale: This definition is related to genetic risk factors, which is a cross-cutting concern across multiple specialties.

extracted_rules.condition_hint: Patient has been treated for breast cancer
extracted_rules.action_hint: Schedule follow-up visits according to recommended frequency
extracted_rules.source_excerpt: The follow-up frequency suggested in the first 5 years is every 6 months or earlier if any symptoms. Subsequent visits could be annual up to10 years and then 2 yearly.
extracted_rules.scope_rationale: This rule is specific to the supportive specialty for breast cancer and outlines the recommended follow-up schedule.

extracted_rules.description: No routine laboratory or radiological investigations
extracted_rules.action_hint: Do not perform routine laboratory or radiological investigations
extracted_rules.source_excerpt: Randomized trials 48,49 have shown that regular follow up laboratory or radiological investigations does not improve survival or quality of life hence they are not recommended.
extracted_rules.scope_rationale: This rule is related to the avoidance of unnecessary tests, which is a cross-cutting concern across multiple specialties.
